info.title: Byte Engine HTTP Inspector API
info.description: Inspect and control a running headed Byte Engine application through its loopback HTTP server. The inspector listens on port 6680 and does not provide authentication. Keep it bound to the loopback interface.

tags.name: Inspection
tags.description: Read runtime entities, registered message payload shapes, publication ranges, and configuration events.

tags.name: Control
tags.description: Send supported runtime messages or request application shutdown.

tags.name: Screenshots
tags.description: Capture renderer sinks and render targets, one image at a time or several from the same frame, as PNG, lossless EXR, or raw bytes.

get.description: Returns factory-created entities known to the shared message bus. Each result includes the numeric handle used as a message target and every complete Rust type name associated with the entity. Use either `type` or its compatibility alias `class` to filter by one complete Rust type name.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Complete Rust type name. Do not send this together with `class`.

parameters.name: class
parameters.description: Compatibility alias for `type`. Do not send both parameters.

200.description: Current entity catalog, or the matching subset when filtered.

get.description: Returns message publication ranges observed since the previous call. This operation drains the shared inspector cursor. It preserves sequence order within each typed route but does not define ordering between routes. Message payloads remain opaque.

200.description: Publication ranges since the previous drain.

post.description: Publishes one registered targeted message to the running application. Query `GET /messages/types` first to discover the accepted protocol names and JSON payload shapes. The request object must contain exactly `type`, `target`, and `payload`. To trigger a named action, resolve its target with `GET /entities?name=<action>` and post `TriggerAction` with a matching input value.

204.description: The message was accepted and published.

400.description: The envelope, message type, target, or reflected payload is invalid.

get.description: Returns every protocol message type currently accepted by `POST /messages`, sorted by `type`. Each `payload` is a cached JSON-oriented descriptor derived from the same Facet shape used to parse posted values. Use object fields and array lengths to build editor controls, and use `required` to decide which object fields the editor must send.

200.description: Registered protocol message names and payload shapes.

get.description: Returns retained configuration requests with the latest state reported by the system that owns each parameter.

500.description: A configuration value could not be serialized.

get.description: Captures one image from a renderer sink. Without `pass` or `target`, the request reads the final swapchain image. Provide only `target` to read a scene-pipeline target after every scene pipeline has recorded, such as `Diffuse Radiance History`, or add `pass` to read a target right after that render pass. Add `previous=true` with a `target` to read the copy of a history target that the previous frame wrote, which is what the current frame's passes read as history. That copy holds no usable data on a sink's first frame or right after a resize. The request waits up to five seconds for a graphics frame to complete. To capture several images from the same frame, use `POST /screenshots`.

parameters.name: pass
parameters.description: Exact render-pass name. Requires `target`, and cannot be combined with `previous`.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Exact target name. Without `pass`, the name of a scene-pipeline target or history target. With `pass`, a target that the pass writes.

parameters.name: previous
parameters.description: Reads the previous frame's copy of a history target. Requires `target` without `pass`.

200.description: One image from the completed graphics frame, encoded in the requested `format`.

X-Byte-Engine-Frame.description: Engine frame number that produced the image.

X-Byte-Engine-Sink.description: Renderer sink index that produced the image.

X-Byte-Engine-Format.description: GHI format the texture is stored in, such as `RGBA16F` or `BGRAu8`.

X-Byte-Engine-Bytes-Per-Row.description: Distance in bytes between rows of a `raw` body, which can include GPU padding. Only `raw` responses include it.

404.description: The sink, render pass, or target was not found, or `previous` names a target that keeps no previous frame.

409.description: The sink is unavailable or the pass name is ambiguous.

429.description: The bounded screenshot request queue is full.

500.description: Screenshot capture or encoding failed. The most likely cause is a target format that the selected `format` cannot encode.

504.description: No graphics frame completed within five seconds.

post.summary: Capture screenshots from the same frame
post.description: Captures up to 16 images, from any sinks and capture points, in one graphics frame, so you can compare targets that belong together. Each capture takes the same fields as the `GET /screenshots` query. The response is `multipart/form-data` with one part per capture, in request order. Each part is named by its zero-based capture index, has a file name built from the capture, and carries the same `Content-Type` and `X-Byte-Engine-*` headers as a single-image response, except `X-Byte-Engine-Frame`, which the response itself carries. If any capture fails, the request fails, and the error message starts with the failing capture index.

200.description: One part per capture, all from the same completed graphics frame.

X-Byte-Engine-Frame.description: Engine frame number that produced the image.

400.description: The request body is malformed, has an unknown field, lists no captures or more than 16, or has an invalid capture.

404.description: The sink, render pass, or target was not found, or `previous` names a target that keeps no previous frame.

409.description: The sink is unavailable or the pass name is ambiguous.

429.description: The bounded screenshot request queue is full.

500.description: Screenshot capture or encoding failed. The most likely cause is a target format that the selected `format` cannot encode.

504.description: No graphics frame completed within five seconds.

delete.description: Publishes an application close request. The HTTP response confirms publication, not process termination.

ScreenshotFormat.name: format
ScreenshotFormat.description: Image encoding. `png` is an 8-bit preview that clamps HDR values to [0, 1]. `exr` is a lossless OpenEXR image that keeps the texture's precision: half floats stay half floats, normalized values become linear 32-bit floats, and `U32` stays `U32`. `raw` returns the texture bytes as the GPU stores them.

ScreenshotCaptureRequest.description: One capture. The fields work like the `GET /screenshots` query parameters.

pass.description: Exact render-pass name. Requires `target`, and cannot be combined with `previous`.

target.description: Exact target name. Without `pass`, the name of a scene-pipeline target or history target. With `pass`, a target that the pass writes.

previous.description: Reads the previous frame's copy of a history target. Requires `target` without `pass`.

format.description: Image encoding. See the `format` query parameter of `GET /screenshots`.

target.description: Stable numeric handle used by targeted inspector messages.

types.description: Complete Rust type names registered for the entity.

type.description: Stable protocol name accepted in the posted message envelope.

PayloadShape.description: Recursive JSON payload descriptor. Scalars use `type` and may include a Rust `format`. Arrays use `items` and optional `length`, `unique`, or `dimensions`. Tuples use `items`. Objects use ordered `fields` with `name`, `required`, `flattened`, and nested `shape`, plus `additional_fields`. Optional values use `shape`; maps use `keys` and `values`; results use `ok` and `error`; enums use `representation`, optional `tag` and `content`, and named `variants`. Recursive and unknown values include `name`.

scope.description: Diagnostic name of the route-owning message scope.

type.description: Complete Rust message type name, including generic arguments.

first_sequence.description: First zero-based publication sequence in this range.

count.description: Number of consecutive publications in this range.

InputValue.description: A reflected action value. The variant must match the action's declared type.

orientation.description: Finite quaternion components in x, y, z, w order. The quaternion must have non-zero length.

Vector3.description: Three finite x, y, and z components.

ConfigurationValue.description: Boolean, signed integer, floating-point, or text configuration value.

ErrorMessage.description: Plain-language error followed by the most likely cause.
